clue.text: Make good a large number of debtors' bills, falsifying accounts?

parts.note: to make good something broken is to mend it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
IOUs are the written notes a debtor hands over promising repayment

explanation.surface: Someone cooks the books by doctoring a huge pile of unpaid bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing someone who is falsifying accounts, i.e. telling lies; the question mark flags that loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lying person gives untruthful versions of events, which is what giving false accounts amounts to.

clue.text: Get excited about one minute defeat?

indicators.note: about means the first word is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: elate is to fill with excitement and joy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sports fan gets worked up about a sudden loss in the final minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IMIN inside the outer word. 'Get excited' looks like the definition, but the answer is a verb for knocking out of a contest, so 'defeat' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock a team out of a competition is to beat it so it plays no further part.

clue.text: Writer fed up with nameless individual

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation N for name is dropped

parts.note: one can mean a single individual, as in 'one of us'

explanation.surface: An author has had enough of some anonymous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF; 'nameless' strips N (name) from ONE, leaving OE. 'fed up' looks like a phrase meaning annoyed, but it is fodder plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Pale actor turned out to be a drama queen

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters have been reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: A wan performer proved to be a real diva offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges the nine letters of PALE ACTOR. 'drama queen' reads as a diva but means a queen in a play, as in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian ruler is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy, so she is a monarch from the stage.

clue.text: Person in commanding position who's to make arrangements?

definitions.meaning: someone in charge who gives commands to others
someone who puts things into a neat sequence or tidies them

explanation.definitionFit: One who gives commands and one who sorts things into sequence are both people who order.

clue.text: Found celebrity tiresome, at first

parts.note: a star is a famous person

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of tiresome is used

explanation.surface: Someone discovered that fame becomes wearisome right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a business or institution is to begin it from nothing.

clue.text: Notices vociferous and controversial writer

indicators.note: vociferous means loud and spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: notices are things one marks or remarks on

explanation.surface: A noisy, divisive author attracts plenty of reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: MARKS and MARX are pronounced the same; Karl Marx wrote Das Kapital.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx's political writings remain hotly disputed, making him a famously divisive author.

clue.text: Mk II version Tom had him writing about?

parts.note: Mk is the usual abbreviation of Mark, as in a model number like Mk II
II is Roman two, and twain is an old word for two

explanation.surface: A second model of something is linked to the author behind Tom's adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' is a link. The definition is cryptic: Tom Sawyer is the character the American author wrote about.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist Samuel Clemens, writing under his pen name, created Tom Sawyer and wrote his adventures.

clue.text: Partygoer with extra bottle, unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its first letter, its opening

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, so having more of it is being braver

explanation.surface: A guest arrives at the party carrying a spare bottle of wine that stays sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a wine bottle but is British slang for nerve; 'unopened' removes the first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to wild all-night dance parties is a clubber who loves a good time.

clue.text: What might provide assistance, landing flier in trouble?

definitions.text: What might provide assistance, landing flier in trouble?

indicators.note: landing in the sense of catching and taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: aid is help or assistance

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the word flier is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pilot in difficulty needs a place that can help him land safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges the flier into IRFIEL and 'landing' takes it in. Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a place that helps a pilot in difficulty get down.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway site is where a pilot in distress can bring the aircraft down safely.

clue.text: To gain recognition, I have put a posh car at the front

indicators.note: at the front says the car and the a come before the other piece

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the classic upmarket car
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A social climber reckons a luxury car parked out front will earn respect.
explanation.walkthrough: RR is the abbreviation for Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it, becoming established and successful, is an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Implicitly bigger case

definitions.meaning: suggesting something has gone up in dimensions
to case is to inspect or examine, as a burglar cases a house

explanation.definitionFit: Assessing a situation is weighing it, and a garment going one larger is a step in dimensions.

clue.text: Revolutionary given contemptuous expression by a right-winger

parts.note: rot is an exclamation dismissing something as nonsense
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A radical gets a sneer from a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks political, but here it means spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turning about an axis is revolving, which is the literal sense of revolutionary.

clue.text: Mum's the word — mafia's leaders twice seen together

indicators.note: twice seen together means the same letters appear two times in a row

parts.note: the leading letters of the word mafia

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about the mob bosses, who appear as a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum's the word' reads as a call for silence; Mum is the definition and 's the word a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal names a child uses for its mother.

clue.text: Drug-habit, in modern parlance?

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, so it can stand for modern
diction is a manner of speaking, as is parlance

explanation.surface: A drug habit is described in contemporary slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'modern parlance' poses as a note on current slang, but the question mark signals the answer is to be read as two words describing up-to-date speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependency on narcotics is the classic form of this compulsion.

clue.text: Rejected seat, reportedly, at the opponents' ground

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a throne is a royal seat
a team playing away is at the other side's ground

explanation.surface: A fan's seat was turned down at the rival club's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: THRONE is pronounced like THROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discarded has been cast off as unwanted.

clue.text: Short of time, town in Cumbria is trying to improve

indicators.note: short of means lacking one letter from the word

parts.note: Workington is a coastal town in Cumbria, the county of the English Lake District

explanation.surface: A Cumbrian town pressed for time is striving to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being busy perfecting something means putting effort into making it better.

clue.text: Bearing up in real case to do with insurance calculations

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another
case means the word real acts as the outer shell

parts.note: actual means real

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: air is one's bearing or demeanour

explanation.surface: Keeping a stiff upper lip over a genuine insurance claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the bearing word backwards to RIA, and 'in ... case' places it within the word for real. 'Bearing up' reads as coping bravely, but it is fodder plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An actuary computes risk and premiums for insurers, and this adjective describes that work.

clue.text: Nut loaf and sausage

parts.note: loaf is British slang for the head, from rhyming slang loaf of bread
banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: A bakery and butcher's order: a nut loaf and a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut loaf' reads as a vegetarian dish, but Nut is the definition. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person, or a rock fan who shakes their skull, is informally called a nutter.

clue.text: Ibsen heroine nursing male better

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as one nurses a baby

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title character of an Ibsen play

explanation.surface: Ibsen's heroine looks after a man who is recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective or verb but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who places wagers is a punter, one who lays bets.

clue.text: Shooter turns and puts ball into goal

indicators.note: turns means the gun's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A striker spins and scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' looks like a footballer but is the Sten gun; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring in football or hockey means sending the ball into the mesh behind the goal line.

clue.text: Supporting right to advertise

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a claim is a right or entitlement to something

explanation.surface: Someone backs the right to publicise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something publicly is to broadcast it far and wide.

clue.text: Lover runs rings round me

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: round means the rings are placed on either side of the next word

parts.note: each ring is the circle-shaped letter O, so two rings give two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suitor goes about encircling the speaker with jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero is a byword for an ardent wooer.

clue.text: Regions in china and Japan etc, off limits?

indicators.note: off limits means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: China, Japan and their neighbours form the Far East

explanation.surface: Asking which parts of East Asia are forbidden to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off limits' looks like 'forbidden', but it strips F and T from FAR EAST. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Zones or districts are parts of a larger territory.

clue.text: Form of insect, odd strain

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of strain are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: A peculiar strain of insect has appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: An instar is a developmental stage of an insect between moults.

clue.text: Unqualified — straight up!

definitions.meaning: complete and absolute, as in pure nonsense
perpendicular, like a vertical cliff face

explanation.definitionFit: Utter nonsense is absolute, and a precipice that rises vertically is steep in the extreme.

clue.text: Unionist politician, Irish, meeting English judge

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish politician meets an English magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee in cricket or tennis adjudicates disputes on the field.

clue.text: Flickering niggled operator at first, having accessed computer

indicators.note: flickering suggests the letters dance about into a new order
at first takes just the opening letter of operator

explanation.surface: A flickering screen irritated the operator when first logging on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flickering' rearranges NIGGLED plus O, the first letter of operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Having entered a password and username, a user has signed on to the system.

clue.text: To some extent, Lisbon nowadays is seen as an old European capital

definitions.text: is seen as an old European capital

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lisbon today is thought of as a historic European capital, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonn was the capital of West Germany until reunification.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonn served as West Germany's seat of government until 1990.

clue.text: Portion of Chinese food bound to go round

parts.note: to bound is to leap or spring
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A takeaway snack is ready to be passed round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crispy fried pancake filled with vegetables is a classic dim sum item.
